title: Why Paul commands a sharp rebuke, and purity belongs to creation
english: Since Paul often teaches and praises gentleness, but found that the Cretans needed the rebuke as a spur, for this reason Paul said, “Rebuke them sharply” (Titus 1:13). Paul writes, “To the pure all things are pure” (Titus 1:15). God made all things pure. But if they are impure, the accusation would touch the one who created them.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Titum u01-rem-early
orientation: Severianus is explaining Paul's instructions to Titus about rebuking the Cretans and about purity, after Paul quoted the Cretan poet's saying.

title: Women called to clerical inheritance
english: And this is what it means: “They profess to know God, but they deny him by their works” (Titus 1:16). Paul showed that he calls women to a share in the clerical inheritance, for he would not have called them reverent in Titus 2:3 otherwise.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Titum u01-rem-mid
orientation: Severianus is commenting on Titus 1:16 and 2:3, explaining that Paul's calling older women reverent shows they are summoned to a clerical inheritance.

title: Integrity of mind and dignity of work
english: In Tit 2:7, Paul took integrity as a matter of the mind, and dignity as a matter of work, so that the teacher may refrain not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Titum u01-rem-close
orientation: Severianus is explaining Paul's instruction in Titus 2:7, distinguishing where integrity and dignity apply.
